title: This Ant's Jaws Snap Shut at 145 mph. It Uses Them to Jump
subject: trap-jaw ant

scenes.text: An ant's jaws close faster than a blink. And it uses them to launch itself.
The trap-jaw ant's mandibles snap shut at up to 64 metres per second, about 145 mph.
The strike lasts about 0.13 milliseconds, roughly 2,300 times faster than a blink.
The jaws accelerate at around 100,000 times gravity, the fastest self-powered strike known.
Hit the ground or an intruder with them, and the ant is flung into the air.
Some jump about eight centimetres up, spinning, long enough to dodge a lizard's tongue.

description:
The trap-jaw ant closes its jaws at up to 145 mph, the fastest self-powered predatory strike recorded, and can use that strike to jump away from danger.
The jaws accelerate at about 100,000 times gravity.
What tiny animal would you least want to cross?
first_comment: The ants can't control where they land. Would you trust a jump like that?
